newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO sees 9 pct return from SFB.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees 9 pct return from SFB.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said its proposed U.S. acquisition, Standard Federal Bancorp (SFB), would generate an initial annualised return of about nine percent.
Executive board chairman Jan Kalff said this was before financing costs on the planned $1.95 billion purchase price.
The cost of financing the deal would amount to a net dividend of 6.5 percent on a planned $750 million preference share issue and four percent on existing funds for the balance.
"The acquisition will, for the greater part, be financed by existing means," Kalff told a news conference.
The Dutch bank said earlier the purchase would add tens of guilder cents to earnings per share.
ABN AMRO's offer of $59 per share values the target bank at 2.1 times book value and 13.9 times annualised profits, excluding non-recurring items, in the first nine months of 1996.
ABN AMRO has 10,981 full time staff in North America, most them at its Lasalle unit in Chicago.
Michigan-based Standard Federal, the 11th largest mortgage originator in the United States, has 3,960 staff.
